Open a vault

Source: R/open_vault.R
open_vault.Rd

Open a connection to a SQLite database

Usage

open_vault(path, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

path

A character string of the path to the SQLite database

verbose

A logical value indicating whether to print messages

Value

A vault_pipe list with two elements, data and db_con, and a database_version attribute.

Details

open_vault() reads the VegVault version of the database from the row of version_control with the highest id and stores it as the database_version attribute. vaultkeepr supports VegVault 1 and 2 (so far, the releases 1.0.0 and 2.0.0). For an older or a newer version, or one that cannot be read as a version number, open_vault() closes the connection and stops with an error. A database without version rows is read as VegVault 1.0.0.

The database is opened read-only: vaultkeepr only reads from it, and a read-only connection guarantees that no query, in vaultkeepr or in user code, changes the file. A statement that writes to the database, such as CREATE TABLE, fails with an error. Temporary tables, for example from dplyr::compute(), still work, because SQLite keeps them outside the file.
